newsitem.title: FRANCE: Grain trade awaits big Pakistan wheat purchase.
newsitem.headline: Grain trade awaits big Pakistan wheat purchase.

text.p: Grain traders are still awaiting news of a key Pakistani wheat purchase on Tuesday, with the U.S. and Australia said to be battling over a total deal covering 500,000 tonnes.

European traders said there were very few clear indications ahead of the U.S. opening, but highlighted talk of aggressive offers from Australia in a tender expected to be finalised in the next few hours.
"The Australians seem to have done a large amount, the rest is probably American," said one trader.
He said no precise figures were available but one unconfirmed estimate had put the Australian share as high as 400,000 tonnes. Others were between 200,000 and 300,000 tonnes.
The share of U.S. white wheat in the deal will depend largely on credit financing, traders said.
A senior U.S. wheat export trader said overnight the maximum amount of wheat Pakistan could buy with its remaining GSM-102 U.S. government financing was 225,000 tonnes.
Pakistan is seeking 500,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat for August 11-September 10 shipment.
Pakistan's embassy in Washington D.C. has said it will announce the awards on Tuesday.
European exporters agreed with U.S. trade estimates of American offers to supply white wheat starting from around $148 per tonne.
U.S. exporters said on Monday that U.S.-origin grain could take half the amount Pakistan was seeking or slightly more.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture last week raised by $25 million the amount of GSM-102 credit guarantees available for sale of U.S. farm goods to Pakistan, boosting Pakistan's 1997 (Oct/Sept) fiscal year allocation to $325 million.
Pakistan is reported to have received offers from the U.S., Australia and Canada.
U.S. traders on Monday estimated the Australian offers in the range of $158 to $159 a tonne.
Canada was said to be offering $147.50, FOB, Pacific ports, for about 50,000 tonnes.
U.S. offers were difficult to pin down but one exporter there pegged them in a range of $148.22 to $149.43, FOB, Pacific Northwest for about 200,000 tonnes of U.S. white wheat.
Another 100,000 tonnes was believed to be on offer at between $149.87 and $150.05.
